Building more on the Zim-SA Test series, it is not just Wiaan Mulder's unbeaten 367 which has grabbed the headlines. Kundai Matigimu, a fast bowler from Zimbabwe, has been fined 15 percent of his match fee and also handed a demerit point, for 'inappropriate and dangerous' conduct on Day 1 of the second Test. There was a ball which Lhuan-dre Pretorius defended back to the bowler, Matigimu, who picked it up and fired a throw back at the batter, hitting him near the wrist. Irrespective of whether this was done deliberately or not, the ICC has monitored it closely and come to the conclusion that it was not within sporting conduct at all. Aggression is good but when not toned, can go out of hand.

Talking about pressure, Zimbabwe have succumbed to incessant pressure against South Africa in the second Test in Bulawayo, losing by an innings and 236 runs inside 8 sessions. Having conceded 626 in the first innings and folding up for 170 inside 43 overs in their own first dig, this was coming, but what would have disappointed the home side is that, it was 153/3 in the second innings. However, half centurion Nick Welch's dismissal triggered a collapse and from 153/3, they folded up for 220. In the morning session, it did seem like the hosts were up for a fight but the Proteas just blew the game open post Lunch. Corbin Bosch finished with 4 scalps while Senuran Muthusamy had a good outing with 3 wickets. Not surprisingly, South Africa clean sweep the series 2-0 but they will not get any WTC points, as this series was not included in the WTC cycle. From Zimbabwe's point of view, they will gain a lot from this experience, before they take on New Zealand in their next Test assignment at home, in the last week of July.

Right then, 286 is the target for Bangladesh and it is definitely gettable given how the pitch has played. However, we have seen in the first two games that there is some added pressure on the chasing team and with Bangladesh not just chasing a win but a maiden series win in Sri Lanka, the pressure will be on them. It should be an entertaining chase with both sides looking to take the bragging rights. Stay tuned.

Taskin Ahmed was the one who put an end to a stellar 124-run stand between Kusal Mendis and Charith Asalanka and that triggered a mini collapse for Sri Lanka as they went from being 224/3 to 259/7 in the next 7 odd overs. Bangladesh let things slip again and the likes of Wanindu Hasaranga and Dushmantha Chameera were able to find a few boundaries right at the death to take the hosts over the 280 mark.

The innings ebbed and flowed for a bit but the Bangladeshi spinners did get a couple of wickets to peg Sri Lanka back to 100/3 in 21 overs but then came a decisive stand between Kusal Mendis and skipper Charith Asalanka. The bowlers looked out of sorts as Mendis and Asalanka piled on the runs, with the former going on to notch up a 6th ODI ton and even the skipper made 58 useful runs before getting out.

Generally, we see some early seam movement in Pallekele, but the Bangladeshi pacers didn't get much from the deck or in the air. However, Tanzim Hasan Sakib got the wicket of Nishan Madushka pretty early on and Bangladesh had something to build on. They couldn't capitalize and Kusal Mendis' aggressive start pushed the visitors onto the back foot and there was a 56-run partnership between Mendis and Pathum Nissanka.

At the toss, we heard Charith Asalanka, the Sri Lankan captain, say that they wanted to put 280 runs on the board and they have done exactly that. The pitch looked to be on the slower side to begin with but it just kept on getting better to bat on. The hosts will feel that they could have surpassed the 300-run mark, given they were 222/3 at one stage but Bangladesh pulled things back a bit with a flurry of wickets in the last 10 overs.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK. Sri Lanka have pressed on the accelerator nicely. The last 9 overs have yielded 47/1 and the boundaries are coming a bit more frequently. Kusal Mendis though, is playing a quizzical type of innings. He started off like a train on fire, but post Powerplay 1, seems to have gone into a shell. Mind you, his strike rate is still decent, at 88 but for a player who started so quickly, you might have expected that to rise to 120. However, he is trying to bat deep. Skipper Asalanka has maintained his good run and is looking good already. Going by the Bumble formula, that is, the opinion of the great David Lloyd, former English commentator, if you have wickets in hand at the end of the 30th over, you can double your score by the 50th. So it does seem like 280-290 is on the cards. Bangladesh are not quite able to put any sustained pressure on the Lankans, as opposed to the second ODI. They are not conceding boundaries or runs like a river but at the same time, are not able to tie down one end consistently. Remember a game in the earlier years, where Shane Watson was facing a bowler, I think Andre Russell, but Russell pulled out of the delivery stride midway. PITCH REPORT - Former Sri Lankan allrounder, FARVEEZ MAHAROOF, has a look at the deck. Does not feel that the pitch looks much dissimilar from the ones dished out in Colombo. Opines that the surface is not that dry but has lot of brown grass that has been rolled in nicely. Feels that the pitch will be very good for batting, especially against the new balls. Feels that we could see some spin in the middle overs. Informs that 8 out of the last 10 ODIs here have been won by the side chasing but you want to bat first here in this heat.

The captain of Bangladesh, Mehidy Hasan Miraz agrees with Asalanka, affirming that the wicket looks good and history says that 280 would be a good score here. But he definitely would want to field first as he reckons that sometimes, the pitches here can spin a bit in the first innings. On the team changes, Mehidy informs that Taskin Ahmed is back and replaces Hasan Mahmud. On the thought of the series being on the line, Miraz says that it is a great opportunity for his side. Adds that his players are excited and hopes that everyone perform and Bangladesh win.

The skipper of Sri Lanka, Charith Asalanka, feels that the pitch looks like the usual ones in Kandy. On a good score on this deck, Asalanka says that he thinks 280 would be a par score. On the feeling of the series being on the line, Charith calls it really interesting. Wants to forget what happened in the previous game and wants to come back hard like any good team. Informs that Sri Lanka are going in unchanged from the previous match.
Another good news. The weather was expected to be iffy but for now, it is bright and sunny. Let's hope the weather stays clear till the end of this grand finale.

The caravan rolls into Kandy for the third and final ODI of the series between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, with the contest tantalisingly poised at 1-1. The Pallekele International Cricket Stadium is all set to host what promises to be a cracking decider. Bangladesh were left ruing a dramatic collapse in the opener, losing 7 wickets for just 5 runs from a winning position, but they bounced back in style to snap a seven-match losing streak in the format. In response to Bangladesh’s 248, Sri Lanka made a steady start at 75 for 1 but then lost wickets at regular intervals. From 170 for 8, Janith Liyanage reignited their hopes, but once he fell, Sri Lanka’s chances went down with him. While Charith Asalanka starred with the bat in the first game, it was Janith Liyanage and Kusal Mendis who made impactful contributions in the second. The hosts will look to Pathum Nissanka and Kamindu Mendis to step up with the bat. With the ball, Wanindu Hasaranga has been the standout performer, but Maheesh Theekshana’s lack of impact is a concern, having picked up just one wicket across the two games. As for Bangladesh, they needed someone to step up in the absence of Taskin Ahmed, who was rested for the previous game, and Tanvir Islam did just that, claiming a five-wicket haul in only his second ODI. The potential return of Taskin will strengthen their pace attack, which will be crucial given Mustafizur Rahman's ongoing struggles with both form and fitness in this series. In the batting department, contributions have come from various individuals, with Jaker Ali, Parvez Hossain Emon, Tanzid Hasan, and Tawhid Hridoy all registering fifties. However, former ODI captain Najmul Hossain Shanto is yet to make a significant impact, and there can not be a better occasion than the series decider for him to come to the party. History beckons for Bangladesh, who have never won an ODI series in Sri Lanka. Can the Tigers script history? Or will Sri Lanka rise to the occasion and deny them once again? We shall find out.
